title: Termination
definition: Termination is the property that an algorithm reaches a defined stopping state for every input covered by its contract.
purpose: Ensure an algorithm does not remain in an endless sequence for contract-valid inputs.
history: Termination is a central part of total correctness reasoning for iterative and recursive computation.
mental_model: A measurable quantity moves toward a bound until the stopping condition becomes true.
analogy: A countdown reaches zero because every tick decreases the remaining count; the analogy fails for algorithms without a single numeric progress measure.
common_mistakes: Writing a stop condition without guaranteed progress
industry_notes: Bounded retries, iteration limits, deadlines, and progress arguments are practical controls related to termination.
ai_notes: AI-generated loops must be checked for reachable stop conditions and progress on every branch.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to name a progress measure, bound, and stopping condition.
exercise_candidates: Repair an algorithm whose progress update is skipped on one branch
